title: Walking away from a lamp post
stem:
At night, Ben walks along a straight path, away from a lamp post.

What happens to the length of the shadow made by that lamp?
key: With a lamp shining down on the ground, the farther away you are, the longer your shadow.

options.text: It gets shorter, because he is moving away from the light.
options.pick: In class, moving away from the torch made the shadow smaller, so it seems to work the same way here.
options.why: That rule is for an object between a torch and a wall. Here the shadow lies on the ground under a lamp above him, and moving away makes it longer.

options.text: It stays the same length, because Ben's height does not change.
options.pick: Ben is the object, and he does not change size.
options.why: The shadow also depends on how far Ben is from the lamp. As the distance grows, the shadow grows.

options.text: It gets longer.
options.pick: Picture the straight line from the lamp, past the top of Ben's head, to the ground. Where does it land as Ben moves away?
options.why: As Ben moves away, the light reaches him at a lower slant. He blocks the light over a longer stretch of ground, so the shadow gets longer.

options.text: It gets shorter, because less light reaches him.
options.pick: Farther from the lamp it is dimmer, so the shadow seems to fade and shrink.
options.why: A shadow's length depends on the straight line from the lamp past his head, not on how bright the light is. Farther away, the line slants more and the shadow is longer.

title: Standing under the lamp
stem:
At night, Ben stands directly under a lamp post.

Where is the shadow made by that lamp?
key: Right under a lamp, the light comes straight down, so the shadow is only a small patch at the feet.

options.text: A small patch around his feet
options.pick: The light comes straight down on him. Which part of the ground does he block?
options.why: The light shines straight down, so Ben blocks only the ground directly under him. The shadow is a small patch at his feet.

options.text: A long shadow stretching in front of him
options.pick: He is as close to the lamp as he can be, so the shadow seems to be at its biggest.
options.why: Close to a lamp above you, the light comes down steeply and the shadow is short. Directly under it, the shadow is only a patch at the feet.

options.text: No shadow at all, because the lamp is directly above him
options.pick: With the light right above, there seems to be nowhere for a shadow to go.
options.why: Ben still blocks the light. Light cannot bend around him to reach the ground under his feet, so there is a small shadow there.

options.text: A shadow on the lamp post
options.pick: The lamp post is the closest thing to him, so the shadow seems to fall on it.
options.why: A shadow forms on the side away from the light. The light is above him, so the shadow is on the ground below him, not on the post.

title: Which way does the shadow point?
stem:
At night, a girl stands on the path to the right of a lamp post.

Which way does her shadow from that lamp point?
key: A shadow always points away from its own light.

options.text: To the left, towards the lamp
options.pick: The lamp is on the left, so the shadow seems to be connected to it.
options.why: The light comes from the left. The girl blocks it, so the dark area is on her right, away from the lamp.

options.text: Straight up, behind her
options.pick: A shadow is often drawn as a shape behind a person.
options.why: The shadow falls on the ground where the light is blocked. Light from the lamp on the left is blocked on her right side.

options.text: It depends on which way she is facing.
options.pick: Your shadow seems to follow you around as you turn.
options.why: Turning around does not move the lamp. The shadow always points away from the light, whichever way she faces.

options.text: To the right, away from the lamp
options.pick: Draw a straight line from the lamp past the girl. It carries on to the right.
options.why: Light travels in straight lines from the lamp. The girl blocks it on the side away from the lamp, so the shadow points to the right.

title: A ball, a torch and a screen
stem:
A ball is placed between a torch and a screen. The ball is moved closer to the torch. The torch and the screen do not move.

What happens to the ball's shadow on the screen?
key: Between a torch and a screen, the closer the object is to the torch, the bigger its shadow.

options.text: It becomes smaller, because the ball is closer to the light.
options.pick: More light near the ball seems to leave a smaller shadow.
options.why: Being closer to the torch makes the ball block more of the spreading light, so the shadow on the screen gets bigger.

options.text: It becomes bigger.
options.pick: Close to the torch, the ball blocks a wider spread of the light.
options.why: Light spreads out in straight lines from the torch. Near the torch, the ball blocks more of that spread, so a bigger area of the screen is in shadow.

options.text: It stays the same size, because the ball is the same size.
options.pick: The ball has not changed, so its shadow seems not to change.
options.why: Shadow size also depends on the distances between the torch, the ball and the screen.

options.text: It stays the same size, but becomes darker.
options.pick: Moving towards the light seems to make the shadow stronger, not bigger.
options.why: The size changes: closer to the torch means a bigger shadow.

title: A fair shadow investigation
stem:
Mei Ling wants to find out how the distance between a torch and a toy affects the size of the toy's shadow on a screen.

Which plan is a fair test?
key: Change only the variable being tested. Keep everything else, including the other distance, the same.

text: the distance between the torch and the toy, and the size of the toy
options.pick: Trying different toys at different distances seems to give more results.
options.why: Two things change at once. If the shadow changes, she cannot tell whether the distance or the toy caused it.

text: the distance between the torch and the toy
options.pick: Changing the toy's size will certainly change the shadow.
options.why: This tests the size of the toy, not the distance asked about.

text: the distance between the torch and the toy
the toy, the torch, and the distance between the toy and the screen
options.pick: Change the one distance being tested. Keep everything else that could change the shadow the same.
options.why: Only the torch-to-toy distance changes, so any change in the shadow must come from that distance.

text: the distance between the toy and the screen
options.pick: This is a distance too, so it seems to fit the question.
options.why: The question is about the distance between the torch and the toy. The toy-to-screen distance is a different variable.

title: Why a shadow forms
stem: Why does a shadow form behind a person standing in sunlight?
key: Light travels in straight lines. A shadow is the area that light cannot reach because something blocks it.

options.text: The person's shape is reflected onto the ground.
options.pick: A shadow has the person's shape, like a reflection.
options.why: A shadow is not a reflection. It is the dark area where light has been blocked.

options.text: Light bends around the person but leaves a dark gap behind them.
options.pick: The edges of a shadow make it look as if light curls around the person.
options.why: Light travels in straight lines. It does not bend around the person; it is simply blocked.

options.text: The sunlight is too weak to reach behind the person.
options.pick: The ground behind the person seems too far for the light to reach.
options.why: The ground around the shadow is brightly lit. The light is blocked by the person, not too weak.

options.text: Light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through the person, so the area behind the person gets no light.
options.pick: Think about the path of the light and what is in its way.
options.why: Light travels in straight lines. The person blocks it, so the light cannot reach the area behind them, and that area is the shadow.

title: A cat walks towards a lamp
stem:
At night, a cat walks along a path towards a street lamp.

What happens to the cat's shadow made by that lamp?
key: With a lamp above, moving closer to it makes the shadow on the ground shorter.

options.text: It gets longer, because the cat is getting closer to the light.
options.pick: Near a torch, shadows get bigger, so it seems the same here.
options.why: That is the torch-and-wall case. With a lamp above shining on the ground, getting closer makes the shadow shorter.

options.text: It gets shorter.
options.pick: Picture the straight line from the lamp past the cat's back to the ground as the cat gets closer.
options.why: Closer to the lamp, the light comes down more steeply, so the cat blocks less ground and the shadow is shorter.

options.text: It stays the same length, because the cat does not change size.
options.pick: The cat is the same size the whole time.
options.why: The distance from the lamp changes the shadow's length, even though the cat's size does not change.

options.text: It moves to the side of the cat facing the lamp.
options.pick: The cat is heading towards the lamp, so its shadow seems to lead the way.
options.why: The shadow is always on the side away from the lamp, so it trails behind the cat.

title: Between two lamp posts
stem:
Siti walks along a straight path from lamp post P to lamp post Q, which are 10 m apart.

When is her shadow made by lamp P the longest?
key: The farther you are from a lamp above you, the longer the shadow it makes.

options.text: When she is next to lamp P
options.pick: Close to the light seems to mean a bigger shadow.
options.why: Right next to lamp P, its light comes almost straight down, so the shadow from P is at its shortest.

options.text: When she is halfway between the two lamps
options.pick: The middle seems to be where things balance out.
options.why: Halfway, she is only 5 m from lamp P. Her shadow from P keeps growing all the way to lamp Q.

options.text: It is the same length all the way.
options.pick: Siti does not change size, so her shadow seems to stay the same.
options.why: Her distance from lamp P changes as she walks, and that changes the length of the shadow.

options.text: When she is next to lamp Q
options.pick: Find where she is farthest from lamp P.
options.why: Next to lamp Q she is 10 m from lamp P, the farthest she gets, so P's light slants most and her shadow from P is longest.

title: A lamp beside a box
stem:
A lamp is placed on the left of a box on a table. It is the only light in the room.

Where is the box's shadow?
key: A shadow forms on the side of the object away from the light.

options.text: On the right of the box
options.pick: Light from the left travels in straight lines. Where can it not reach?
options.why: The box blocks the light coming from the left, so the area on its right gets no light.

options.text: On the left of the box, between the box and the lamp
options.pick: The shadow seems to belong near the light that makes it.
options.why: The area between the lamp and the box is lit. The shadow is on the far side, away from the lamp.

options.text: Only directly under the box
options.pick: Objects often seem to have their shadow underneath them.
options.why: The light comes from the side, so the box blocks it on its right, not only underneath.

options.text: There is no shadow, because the light goes around the box.
options.pick: The table around the box is bright, so the light seems to get everywhere.
options.why: Light travels in straight lines and cannot bend around the box, so there is a shadow on its right.

title: Moving a toy towards the wall
stem:
A toy is placed between a torch and a wall. The toy is moved away from the torch, towards the wall. The torch and the wall do not move.

What happens to the toy's shadow on the wall?
key: Between a torch and a screen, the farther the object is from the torch, the smaller its shadow.

options.text: It becomes bigger, because the toy is nearer the wall.
options.pick: Nearer the wall seems to mean a bigger shape on the wall.
options.why: Nearer the wall means farther from the torch, so the toy blocks less light and the shadow shrinks.

options.text: It stays the same size, because the toy is the same toy.
options.pick: The toy has not changed, so the shadow seems not to change.
options.why: The distances between torch, toy and wall also decide the shadow's size.

options.text: It becomes smaller.
options.pick: Farther from the torch, the toy blocks less of the spreading light.
options.why: Light spreads out in straight lines. Away from the torch, the toy blocks a narrower part of it, so its shadow on the wall is smaller.

options.text: It becomes bigger, because the toy is farther from the light.
options.pick: Walking away from a lamp makes a shadow longer, so this seems the same.
options.why: That is the lamp-and-ground case. With a torch and a wall, moving the object away from the torch makes its shadow smaller.

title: Testing the size of an object
stem:
Ravi wants to find out how the size of a card affects the size of its shadow on a screen.

Which set-up is a fair test?
key: Change only the variable being tested, here the size of the card. Keep the torch and both distances the same.

options.text: Cards of different sizes, each placed at a different distance from the torch
options.pick: Every card is tested, so it seems complete.
options.why: Two things change at once. A shadow could change because of the distance, not the size.

options.text: Cards of different sizes, each placed the same distance from the same torch and the same screen
options.pick: Only the card's size should change.
options.why: With the torch and both distances kept the same, any difference in the shadow comes from the size of the card.

options.text: The same card placed at different distances from the torch
options.pick: Moving the card clearly changes the shadow.
options.why: This tests distance, not the size of the card.

options.text: Cards of different sizes and shapes, each placed the same distance from the torch
options.pick: The distances are kept the same, which is what a fair test needs.
options.why: The shape changes as well as the size, so the effect of size alone cannot be found.

title: A puppet show results table
stem:
A pupil moved a torch closer to a puppet. The puppet and the screen did not move. Her results are shown.

What can she conclude?
figure:
Distance between torch and puppet (cm)Height of shadow on screen (cm)
5010
3015
2022
key: Read the table in one direction: as the distance gets smaller, the shadow gets bigger.

options.text: The closer the torch is to the puppet, the smaller the shadow.
options.pick: Close to the light seems to mean less shadow.
options.why: The table shows the opposite: at 20 cm the shadow is 22 cm, its biggest.

options.text: The size of the shadow depends only on the size of the puppet.
options.pick: The puppet decides the shape of the shadow.
options.why: The puppet did not change, yet the shadow changed. The distance made the difference.

options.text: She cannot conclude anything, because she changed the distance.
options.pick: Changing something during an experiment seems to spoil it.
options.why: The distance is the variable she meant to change. Everything else stayed the same, so the test is fair.

options.text: The closer the torch is to the puppet, the bigger the shadow.
options.pick: Follow the table downwards: the distance goes down while the shadow goes up.
options.why: From 50 cm to 20 cm, the shadow grows from 10 cm to 22 cm. Closer torch, bigger shadow.

title: A hand on the wall
stem:
A torch shines on a hand held in front of a wall, and a clear shadow of the hand appears on the wall.

Which explains the shadow?
key: A shadow forms where an object blocks light that travels in straight lines.

options.text: The hand blocks the light, which travels in straight lines.
options.pick: Think about the path of the light from the torch to the wall.
options.why: The light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through the hand, so the part of the wall behind the hand gets no light.

options.text: Light bends around the hand, leaving a dark shape.
options.pick: The shadow has smooth edges, as if light curled around.
options.why: Light travels in straight lines. It is blocked by the hand, not bent around it.

options.text: The wall reflects the shape of the hand.
options.pick: The shadow is hand-shaped, like a mirror image.
options.why: A shadow is not a reflection. It is the area where the hand stops the light.

options.text: The torch gives out darkness where the hand is.
options.pick: The dark patch seems to come from the torch.
options.why: A torch only gives out light. The dark patch is simply where light cannot reach.
